name: 六级模拟卷 · 第二套

writing.prompt:
Part I Writing (30 minutes)

Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "The ability to speak well in public is no longer optional." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop the essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.ideas: 审题思路:引句立场明确——公共表达已成必修能力。写法:① 首段肯定引句并解释原因(表达的场景从课堂延伸到职场/网络);② 论证段:举例课堂展示、求职面试、线上会议,对比有能力者与回避者的差距;③ 方法段:公开演讲可以刻意练习(课堂发言、录音复盘、参加社团);④ 结尾呼应引句。
writing.model:
The ability to speak well in public is no longer optional. From classroom presentations and job interviews to online meetings and short videos, a stage of some kind waits for almost everyone, and those who freeze on it are often judged by their worst five minutes rather than their best qualities.
Public speaking matters because ideas have no value until they reach an audience. A brilliant project defended in a trembling voice may lose to an ordinary one presented with clarity and confidence. Employers know this: in interviews, they are not only listening to answers but watching how calmly a candidate organizes thoughts under pressure.
The encouraging news is that speaking is a craft, not a gift. It improves with deliberate practice: volunteering for class presentations, recording oneself and reviewing the playback, or joining a speech club where mistakes are cheap and feedback is immediate. Nerves never disappear completely, but experienced speakers learn to turn them into energy.
In a world where everyone carries a microphone, staying silent is a costly choice. Students who train their voices now are not merely polishing a skill; they are opening the door through which all their other abilities must pass.
writing.notes: 亮点表达:freeze on it(在台上僵住)/judged by their worst five minutes(以最差的五分钟被评判)/a craft, not a gift(是技艺而非天赋)/mistakes are cheap(试错成本很低)/opening the door through which all other abilities must pass(其他能力展示的必经之门)。结尾隐喻升华是六级范文高分收束法。

listening.intro: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
listening.questions:
1. Why is the woman looking for a new flat?
A) Her workplace has moved to another city.
B) Her landlord is raising the rent by twenty percent.
C) Her roommates are moving abroad.
D) Her lease requires her to buy furniture.

2. What does the man say about sharing a flat?
A) It should be avoided at all costs.
B) It only suits students with few belongings.
C) Written rules about quiet hours and chores save friendships.
D) It always leads to arguments about cleaning.

3. What does the man advise checking before signing a contract?
A) The neighbor's taste in music.
B) Utilities, deposit refunds and repair duties.
C) The color of the curtains.
D) The distance to the nearest cinema.

4. How should the woman judge whether an area is safe at night?
A) Read fifty online reviews carefully.
B) Ask the landlord directly.
C) Visit twice and talk to a neighbor.
D) Check the local news website.
listening.analysis:
1. 细节题。女士开场:my landlord is raising the rent by twenty percent, I can't afford that,选 B。
2. 观点题。男士: set clear rules from day one, a written agreement about quiet hours and chores saves most friendships,对应 C。
3. 细节题。男士列清单:whether utilities are included, how the deposit is refunded, and who fixes a broken heater,即 B。
4. 细节题。Visit the area twice, once in daylight and once after dark. Talk to a neighbor...,对应 C。

listening.intro: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the passage you have just heard.
listening.questions:
5. What do doctors in some countries now do?
A) They prescribe a walk in the park.
B) They build parks near hospitals.
C) They forbid patients to use phones.
D) They plant trees with patients.

6. What gap exists in the distribution of urban green space?
A) The suburbs have no parks at all.
B) Downtown areas where land is expensive have the fewest parks.
C) Parks exist only for children.
D) All parks are located in poor neighborhoods.

7. What are pocket parks?
A) Miniature parks built inside shopping malls.
B) Greenery squeezed into gaps between buildings.
C) Private gardens open by appointment.
D) Parking lots turned into playgrounds.
listening.analysis:
5. 细节题。原文 Doctors in some countries can now prescribe a walk in the park,选 A。
6. 细节题。Downtown areas, where land is expensive, often have the fewest parks,而郊区大草坪,选 B。A/C/D 均曲解原文。
7. 词义细节题。Pocket parks squeeze greenery into the gaps between buildings,对应 B。D 说的是 parking lots 被改造成绿地,但 pocket park 的定义是建筑间隙,干扰项辨析。

listening.intro: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the recording you have just heard.
listening.questions:
8. According to the speaker, why are many apps free?
A) Because companies love their users.
B) Because users' attention is sold to advertisers.
C) Because governments pay for them.
D) Because developers work for free.

9. What does research on task switching reveal?
A) Interruptions have no lasting effect.
B) The mind needs many minutes to regain full depth after an interruption.
C) Students study better with phones nearby.
D) Notifications improve comprehension.

10. What is the first step to protect attention?
A) Relying purely on willpower.
B) Buying an expensive alarm clock.
C) Designing the environment, such as keeping the phone in another room.
D) Downloading fewer apps only.

11. What does the quote "we become what we pay attention to" imply?
A) Attention habits shape who we are.
B) Everyone should become a philosopher.
C) Watching lectures changes one's major.
D) Paying attention costs money.
listening.analysis:
8. 细节题。开篇 you are not the customer; you are the product. Your attention is sold to advertisers,选 B。
9. 细节题。原文 after an interruption the mind needs many minutes to return to its full depth,且手机在旁(即使屏幕朝下)成绩更差,选 B。
10. 细节题。第一步 design your environment instead of relying on willpower,例子即把手机放到另一个房间,选 C。A 与原文相反。
11. 推理题。引文的含义:注意力的去向塑造人生,故应慎重选择,对应 A。B/D 属字面游戏。

reading.title: Section D 仔细阅读
reading.passage:
On a former factory roof in Paris, rows of tomatoes, strawberries and salad greens now grow under glass, tended by farmers who ride an elevator to work. Urban farming, once dismissed as a hobby for gardening enthusiasts, is quietly becoming an industry, with rooftop greenhouses, vertical plant walls and underground farms appearing in cities from Singapore to Chicago.
The appeal is easy to understand. Food grown on a roof travels meters, not thousands of kilometers, which means fresher vegetables, lower transport emissions and less spoilage. Rooftop farms also insulate the buildings beneath them, reducing heating and cooling bills, and they turn unused gray space into green space that cools the street below.
Yet city farming is no magic solution. Start-up costs are high: waterproofing, structural reinforcement and lighting can swallow hundreds of thousands of dollars before the first seed sprouts. Energy is another awkward question, because crops under LED lights may consume more electricity than traditional farms use from the sun. And the harvest is limited by definition: a city cannot feed itself from its roofs, however many it plants.
The most sensible conclusion is to see urban farms as one layer in a smarter food system rather than a replacement for rural agriculture. Where they truly shine is in shortening supply chains for perishable greens, in teaching city children where food comes from, and in proving that concrete need not be the last word. A city that grows even a small share of its own food is a city that takes both its meals and its future a little more seriously.
reading.questions:
12. What does the Paris example in Paragraph 1 illustrate?
A) The high cost of urban rent.
B) Urban farming turning into a real industry.
C) The decline of factory buildings.
D) French taste in vegetables.

13. Which benefit of rooftop farms is NOT mentioned?
A) Fresher vegetables with less spoilage.
B) Lower transport emissions.
C) Insulation that cuts energy bills.
D) Increased property taxes.

14. What awkward question does urban farming face?
A) LED lighting may use more electricity than sunlight farming.
B) Rooftop crops taste worse than rural ones.
C) Farmers refuse to ride elevators.
D) Cities lack seeds in winter.

15. Why can't a city feed itself from its roofs?
A) Roofs are too small by definition.
B) The harvest is limited compared with a whole city's needs.
C) Laws forbid selling roof-grown food.
D) Rooftops are reserved for solar panels.

16. What is the passage's conclusion about urban farms?
A) They will replace rural agriculture soon.
B) They are a marketing trick of tech companies.
C) They are one valuable layer of a smarter food system.
D) They should be limited to schools.
reading.analysis:
12. 例证作用题。首段例子引出 urban farming ... quietly becoming an industry,选 B。
13. 细节题(排除法)。第二段列了 freshness/transport emissions/spoilage 与 insulate ... reducing heating and cooling bills,唯独没提 D 房产税。
14. 细节题。第三段 Energy is another awkward question ... LED lights may consume more electricity,选 A。
15. 推理题。the harvest is limited by definition: a city cannot feed itself from its roofs,即产量相对整城需求有限,选 B。
16. 主旨题。末段 see urban farms as one layer in a smarter food system rather than a replacement,选 C。

translation.prompt:
Part IV Translation (30 minutes)

Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English.

近年来,全民健身已上升为一项国家战略。在城市里,健身步道、社区健身房和体育公园不断增多,越来越多的人下班后跑步、骑车或跳广场舞。线上健身课程的兴起,使人们在家锻炼成为可能。政府鼓励学校保证学生每天锻炼一小时。人们普遍认为,健康的国民是国家最宝贵的财富。
translation.reference: In recent years, national fitness has been elevated to a national strategy. In cities, fitness trails, community gyms and sports parks keep increasing, and more and more people run, cycle or dance in squares after work. The rise of online fitness classes has made it possible for people to exercise at home. The government encourages schools to ensure that students exercise for at least one hour every day. It is widely believed that healthy citizens are a nation's most valuable asset.
translation.notes: 要点解析:① "上升为战略"译为 be elevated to a strategy,被动语态突出政策动作;② "不断增多"用 keep increasing 表持续动态;③ "使……成为可能"高频句式 make it possible for sb. to do;④ "保证学生每天锻炼一小时"用 ensure that 从句,注意时间状语 at least one hour every day 的完整表达;⑤ "人们普遍认为"经典译法 It is widely believed that...,六级翻译几乎必会;⑥ 末句健康国民 = healthy citizens,财富 = asset(单数更地道)。
